title: Optimized PR Workflow — 200-line target, conventional commits, stacking
content:
## PR WORKFLOW STANDARDS (Researched 2026-07-29)

### SIZE LIMITS
- Target: 100-200 lines per PR (Google standard)
- Soft limit: 400 lines (review quality cliff at 200-400)
- Hard limit: never exceed 600 lines
- PRs under 200 lines: 75%+ defect detection
- PRs over 1000 lines: 31% defect detection (rubber-stamping)
- 50-line PRs merge within hours; 500+ line PRs take 9 days average

### COMMIT CONVENTIONS
- feat(scope): new feature
- fix(scope): bug fix
- refactor(scope): structural change, no behavior change
- docs(scope): documentation
- test(scope): tests
- chore(scope): build, config, deps
- Keep subject line under 50 chars, lowercase, no period

### MERGE STRATEGY
- Squash merge for most PRs (one commit = one PR)
- Merge commit only when individual commits matter
- Delete branch after merge

### WORKFLOW
- 1 PR = 1 purpose (one sentence to explain)
- Separate refactoring from feature work
- Use draft PRs for early direction, NOT for infinite building
- Self-review (Files Changed tab) before marking ready
- No force-push after review starts
- Stacked PRs when dependencies exist (refactor → feature)
- PR lifecycle target: under 24h from first commit to merge

### ANTI-PATTERNS
- Giant PRs (800+ lines) — reviewer surrenders
- Mixed PRs (refactor + feature + typo) — signal lost in noise
- Empty descriptions — no 'why', no 'verification'
- Force-push mid-review — loses reviewer context
- 'While I'm at it' changes — separate PRs for unrelated work
